title: 2026-09-02-private-vpc-ops-healthcheck-kernel-quantization-sync
summary: Weekly POC sync covering VPC connectivity, routing fallbacks, kernel/quantization rolling upgrade plan, recent latency regressions and next-step benchmarking. Agreement to run controlled KV-cache and quant profiles, security doc follow-up and schedule a canary roll next Tuesday.
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-09-02 18:45 PT
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Alex (Redwood SE), Riley (Redwood Support), Priya (Solstice SRE), Tomás (ML Ops), Evan (Network), Sara (Security)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have about an hour, um so quick agenda — check recent perf numbers, routing incidents, and the kernel/quant canary.
[00:18] Priya: yeah thanks, Maya. we saw a couple of 95th percentile blips this week after the quant profile change, wondering if that matches what you saw on your side.
[00:30] Alex: right — we correlated some of the spikes to KV cache misses and a small hot path in the new kernel path. not a complete regression but some outliers.
[00:42] Tomás: we pushed the quant profile to staging on Wed, and then production saw the increase Thu morning. tokens per second dropped about 7% on longer sequences — users noticed latency.
[00:56] Evan: on networking side, there was a transient egress route flapping at 3am — BGP-style thing with our partner edge, not Redwood, but it made fallback policies more likely to fire.
[01:10] Riley: got it. we're seeing the fallback routing engaged twice then; that def increases tail latency while it warms caches.
[01:25] Sara: quick sec — from security perspective we need an updated audit log of the kernel rollout and the canary metrics, plus confirmation of KMS usage for key material.
[01:37] Maya: yes we'll share the rollout artifacts, the canary graph, and KMS attestations. sharing links after the call — will put in the notes.
[01:50] Priya: great. can you remind us of the canary plan? we want a clear rollback trigger.
[02:01] Alex: sure — plan is: canary on 5% traffic for 24 hours, monitor 95/99th latency, token cost, and quality diffs from eval prompt set. rollback if 95th latency regresses >10% or if quant quality drops per the eval runner (we'll tie to prompt set thresholds).
[02:20] Tomás: who runs the eval runner on our side? we have a light harness but can integrate Redwood's eval set.
[02:31] Alex: Redwood SE team will provide the eval harness; Tomás or Priya can run it in your staging with the quant profile. we'll supply the gold prompts and scoring script.
[02:45] Priya: ok that works. next, on KV cache warm-up — do you recommend pre-warming prefixes for our chat flows?
[02:55] Alex: yes for predictable UX we recommend prefix prewarm for top 20 intents. for other traffic, smart prefix caching should help but we've seen that some long-tail queries still cause cold-start token bursts.
[03:12] Evan: what's the impact on cost for pre-warm? we need to justify to finance.
[03:20] Maya: cost up modestly for pre-warm but you gain a lot in tail latency reductions; Redwood Optimize can give modeled delta — we'll attach that sheet.
[03:32] Tomás: on the kernel upgrade itself — version 2.14 you mentioned — any known compatibility issues with our on-prem inference host?
[03:44] Alex: 2.14 changed scheduling heuristics and introduced a new quant code path; most customers are fine but with older NV drivers you can hit a fallback to CPU paths. we flagged that in the release notes. Evan, can you confirm driver build on your hosts?
[03:58] Evan: we're on NVIDIA driver 520.61, which should be OK, but one box is still 510 — I'll patch that.
[04:06] Priya: timeline for kernel roll?
[04:10] Maya: propose canary Tue 2026-09-08, full rollout Thu if canary is green. that gives you time to patch drivers.
[04:20] Sara: also need a signed SSO/SAML config doc for audit — our compliance team wants it before the full roll.
[04:28] Maya: we'll put SSO doc in the security packet.
[04:32] [05:00] — 10 minute segment where teams discuss log collection, with some cross-talk and minor mis-attributions: 
[05:00] Tomás: question — in the event of routing fallback, do you preserve headers for tracing?
[05:10] Riley: yes we preserve trace-id and route metadata but occasionally some proxies strip unusual headers, so we log both route and ingress edge ID.
[05:21] Priya: perfect.
[05:25] [12:08] Alex: we ran a quick bench overnight on KV miss rates — attaching the spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/pilot/solstice/kv-bench-0902.csv (link shared). numbers show miss penalty ~90ms for your average sequence length, which aligns with observed 95th spikes.
[12:30] Priya: interesting. so if we prewarm top-20 prefixes latency improves ~60ms?
[12:40] Alex: roughly, yes. also quant mitigations are possible — different quant profiles trade cost vs precision; we tried q4_0 vs q5_hybrid and saw smaller tail with q5_hybrid at slightly higher token CPU.
[13:02] Tomás: can you summarize quality delta between q4_0 and q5_hybrid?
[13:10] Alex: q5_hybrid keeps logits better on long context, so fewer hallucinations on clinical prompts; absolute BLEU-like score improved ~1.8 points in our eval. but again depends on your prompt mix.
[13:28] Sara: from security again, do these quant profiles change how we must handle keys?
[13:36] Maya: no, quant is model runtime, KMS usage for encryption remains same.
[13:41] Evan: network note — we also saw a jitter pattern when fallback policy engaged because the fallback route squeezes through partner edge with smaller MTU; we'll open ticket with partner.
[13:55] Priya: any immediate mitigations?
[14:00] Alex: temporary mitigation is to increase timeout thresholds for the affected route and rely on cache prewarm. longer term partner edge fix.
[14:12] [21:48] Short interruptions while teams coordinate driver patch windows and schedule maintenance.
[21:48] Priya: we'll plan driver updates Fri night window.
[21:55] Tomás: and we'll run Redwood's eval harness in staging Thur-Fri.
[22:04] Riley: I'll send the canary dashboard template and the automated alerts threshold configuration.
[22:12] Maya: ok moving to runbook — if canary fails we immediate rollback and open a postmortem. Do we want Redwood to take the rollback or Solstice?
[22:25] Tomás: prefer Redwood do the rollback for speed but we'll need transparent logs and perhaps a Blue/Green toggle accessible to our SRE.
[22:36] Alex: that's fine — we can hand the toggle to your team through the console with RBAC scoped to your SRE group.
[22:44] Priya: good.
[22:48] [30:10] Quality discussion — some transcript noise and misheard words: 'quant' occasionally transcribed as 'canton'.
[30:10] Alex: small note on eval set coverage — if you have domain-specific prompts (e.g., discharge summaries) send them to us we'll augment the eval set so regressions are meaningful.
[30:26] Tomás: will do. also request: include the long tail chat logs anonymized so we can see real prompt distribution.
[30:34] Sara: legal requires an NDA addendum for production logs in eval; we'll route through our legal.
[30:42] Maya: understood. we'll prepare the addendum template.
[30:48] [43:05] Near end we cover action items and next steps:
[43:05] Maya: recap — Alex to run controlled bench with q4_0 vs q5_hybrid, attach spreadsheet; Evan to patch drivers and report; Priya/Tomás to run eval harness in staging; Riley to share canary dashboard and RBAC toggle setup; Maya to share security packet and SSO doc.
[43:25] Priya: thanks, if we can meet same time next week to review canary results.
[43:33] Maya: yes same time next Wed would work but note canary planned Tue so earlier is possible.
[43:40] Tomás: prefer Thurs 18:30 PT for a short post-canary sync.
[43:46] Maya: ok Thurs 2026-09-10 18:30 PT then.
[43:52] Final quick clarifications, a bit of crosstalk as folks drop.
[44:10] Sara: please include SOC2 scope doc and audit log sample in the security packet.
[44:18] Maya: will do.
[44:22] [61:00] End of call — thanks everyone, notes and links to be emailed.
